facts.activity_file: proving dead and testing for zero energy

control_failures.control_label: identification of every energy source for the task
mechanical support of a load during maintenance access

facts.site: Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop
facts.title: unplanned release of electrical energy at P-9501

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 3 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control ENERGY_SOURCE_IDENTIFICATION: the identification of every energy source for the task was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

Control LOAD_SUPPORT_FOR_MAINTENANCE: the mechanical support of a load during maintenance access was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Restore the identification of every energy source for the task on P-9501 and PT-9501 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in applying and verifying an isolation, specifically proving dead and testing for zero energy. P-9501 (dewatering pumps) is in service for pit dewatering. The task proceeded during routine operation while the identification of every energy source for the task was in place but did not perform. The electrical energy involved is held as HV switchgear, and the recorded presentation was shock, arc flash, unplanned energisation.
response.summary: On 10 September 2005 a near hit was recorded on P-9501 and PT-9501 at Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop during routine operation; electrical energy held as HV switchgear was not released.
